thread:
maya: Hey team — customer Brightline in EU-dedicated pool is reporting intermittent 429s + auth errors during inference bursts since last night. P95 latency also jumps. Can someone triage?

sam: Posting initial reproducer and a short timeline. saw ~200 429s over 30m window starting 2612343200. customer says it only hits when they run a 4k-token sequence with model: redwood-13b-8k.

lee: Can you paste the API error body?

maya: Sure — from their app logs: ```json
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","code":429,"message":"quota exceeded for model redwood-13b-8k on pool eu-dedicated-2"}```

sam: Also saw intermittent auth failures: ```curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \ \n https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-8k","input":"..."}'```

andrew: Those auth errors — are they 401 or 403?

maya: 401 once in a while, but mostly 429. 401s look like a transient token validation failure; customer uses rotating short-lived keys via our SDK.

sophie: Important note: customer is on a dedicated pool but not single-tenant nodes. They have MIG slices (1g.5gb, 2g.10gb) mixed on the same host. Could be a VRAM pressure / eviction causing our auth path to slow and token validation timeouts -> 401 then retried into 429s.

eng-runtime: @maya can you grab the node id and pack logs? Also run a quick k6 to repro if possible.

maya: Node ids from their report: node-5432, node-5433. Customer attached runtime logs: ```
[2026-02-28T03:12:34Z] model-serving: alloc failed: insufficient device memory for allocation 1.1GB on MIG 1g.5gb
[2026-02-28T03:12:34Z] kvcache: evict candidate 0x7f8c, evicted 24MB
[2026-02-28T03:12:35Z] auth-proxy: token-check latency 4200ms
[2026-02-28T03:12:35Z] http: response 429 path=/v1/generate customer=brightline
```

sam: That kvcache eviction + token-check latency looks suspicious. When device memory pressure hits, we thrash KV cache and blockers push request queue depth up -> auth proxy timeouts.

lee: Can you share nvidia-smi and MIG layout?

maya: nvidia-smi excerpt customer-provided: ```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        MIG  Profiles | Memory-Usage |
|  0  A100-SXM4    1g.5gb,2g.10gb |  92% / 40GB  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

andrew: Two different MIG profiles on same host with high aggregate usage — classic fragmentation. If one slice tries to allocate bumping the whole host LRU, other slices get squeezed.

sophie: Steps I'm proposing: 1) repro in staging using same model + sequence length against node-5432 snapshot; 2) enable per-slice mem reservation (temporary) OR move Brightline to a less-fragmented node; 3) monitor auth-proxy latency and kvcache evict rate.

eng-runtime: I can reproduce a similar pattern locally by simulating two tenants on different MIG slices with one running a long context. Repro steps: ```bash
# spawn background hog on slice A
runtime-hog --node node-5432 --slice 1g.5gb --alloc 6g &
# run load against slice B
ab -n 1000 -c 8 -p payload.json https://dedicated.eu.redwood/v1/generate
```
Observations: 1) p95 tokens escalate, 2) auth check latencies spike to >3s, 3) 429 returned after our internal request timeout threshold.

maya: Customer wants a mitigation ASAP — they asked for a config change or a move.

sam: Short-term mitigation options: - bump their dedicated assignment to single-slice node (single-tenant if available) - lower their model variant to the 8k->4k or 6B variant during burst windows - increase autoscale headroom to pre-warm more slices (but this costs money)

lee: Ops-level quick fix: we can patch routing policy to prefer nodes tagged "low-fragmentation" for this customer until we re-layout MIG partitions. I'll need approval from infra to evict a few VMs.

andrew: Long-term: better packing algorithm to avoid mixing small/large MIG profiles and a per-node global memory guard to keep auth path & control-plane working under VRAM pressure. Also add KV cache admission backpressure to avoid LRU avalanche.

sophie: For the ticket, we should collect: - exact times of 429/401 - node ids + MIG profiles - nvidia-smi snapshots - kvcache eviction metrics - token-check latencies - customer workload (seq len, batch size)

maya: I've requested that from Brightline and attached a trace. They granted permission to move them to a different node.

eng-runtime: I'll prepare a short runbook to move tenant -> new node and how to verify it's stable: \n1) schedule move within maintenance window\n2) rebind tenant to node-6001 (low-frag)\n3) monitor: kvcache evictions, auth-proxy p95, http 429 rate\n4) if still present, escalate to eng-sre for node-level dump and HSM logs

sam: Adding a temporary customer-facing note: "We're investigating elevated 429s for some dedicated customers caused by GPU memory fragmentation on mixed-MIG hosts. Possible mitigation: a short maintenance move to a less-fragmented node or switching to a smaller model during bursts." :memo:

maya: I'll update the support ticket with the suggested mitigation and ETA. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0457 linked to support-82721. Assigned: eng-runtime, eng-sre.

eng-runtime: Following up — after moving Brightline to node-6001 (single-profile 2g.10gb packing) their 429s dropped to zero over 45m, auth-proxy p95 fell from 2.8s -> 180ms. Closing provisional mitigation. Still tracking for root cause on node-5432.

maya: Customer confirmed decreased errors and signed off on maintenance. Closing ticket after root cause RCA.

sophie: Filed RFC for packing change and guard rails: FP-2026-mig-fragmentation.

andrew: Good catch. We'll use this as a template for similar dedicated pool escalations.

maya: Closing thread.
